name: Martyrdom of Jan Hus and Hussite Movement
summary: The Council of Constance burns Czech reformer Jan Hus at the stake despite an imperial safe-conduct. Outrage in Bohemia ignites a mass religious-national movement; the Hussite Wars (1419–1434) repel five successive papal crusades and establish a tolerated 'Utraquist' Czech church for decades.

_quarry.structural_significance: First successful armed defiance of papal authority in Christendom; demonstrates that vernacular-language reformist religion plus battlefield innovation (wagenburg tactics) can defeat conventional crusading armies. Direct intellectual precursor to Luther.
